note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address and lighting answer below comes from one City of Huntington Beach page, its Park Amenities list, where the pickleball block is four lines long and its heading settles the lighting for all four parks at once. The City's Tennis & Pickleball Information page adds the community-centre addresses and the hours of the lighted tennis courts, which belong to tennis and not to these. Where the City is silent - on hours, on price, on surface, on parking - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: Huntington Beach publishes nothing about parking at any of these four parks. The word does not appear in the pickleball block of the City's Park Amenities page, which gives each venue exactly one line - a name, a street address and a count - and it does not appear on the Tennis & Pickleball Information page either. This site does not fill that gap from a map. What the same amenities page does state is which of the four parks has a restroom, and it names three: Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park all appear under "CITY PARKS WITH A RESTROOM". Boardwalk Park does not, and that absence is recorded here as a silence rather than a no, because a list of parks with restrooms is not a list of parks without them. The rest of each park's amenity listings gives a rough sense of scale. Edison and Marina each carry a basketball court, a handball court, a sports field, tennis courts and a walking loop; Worthy has a basketball court, a picnic table or shelter, a sports field and a walking loop; Boardwalk is listed for an exercise course and a volleyball court and nothing else. The planning fact that matters more than parking here is light. The City states that none of these courts is lit, so every visit is a daylight visit, and the session ends when the sun does.
slots.peak_hours: The City publishes no hours for its pickleball courts, no busy periods, no rotation rule and no league night. What it publishes instead is a single parenthesis that does the work of a schedule: the heading over all four venues reads "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Thirteen courts, four parks, and not one of them usable after dark. That single parenthesis turns the whole question of timing into a question of daylight. A weekday evening game is possible here in June and not in December, and the City has told you so without writing a single opening time. The trap to avoid is the tennis page. The City's Tennis & Pickleball Information page lists lighted tennis courts at two of these same parks - "Edison Community Park (ECC)* 21377 Magnolia Street Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" and "Marina Park (MCP)* 5562 Cross Drive Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" - and a reader who finds a ten o'clock closing time at the address of a pickleball venue could be forgiven for assuming it applies. It does not. Those lines sit under the heading "Lighted Tennis Courts & Handball/Racquetball Courts", and the pickleball courts at the same addresses are, in the City's own words on its other page, without lighting. The tennis page does say one useful thing about organised play: OC Racquet Sports runs clinics the City describes as serving "your tennis or pickleball goals", with "over 50 classes offered each week", registered through the City's SANDS system or at a community centre, with a rain hotline. When the pickleball classes happen, and on which park's courts, the page does not say.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface anywhere in its pickleball record. Each venue gets one line on the Park Amenities page, and that line holds a name, an address and a number of courts; there is no word for what the courts are made of, whether they are dedicated or painted onto something else, or how they are kept. This site does not describe a surface the operator has not described. What the amenities page does make clear, by the way it is organised, is that pickleball in Huntington Beach is counted separately from tennis. The pickleball heading and the tennis heading are different lists with different parks on them: Edison Park and Marina Park appear on both, while Worthy Park and Boardwalk Park appear under pickleball and not under tennis. So at two of the four venues the pickleball courts sit in a park that also has tennis courts, and at the other two they do not. Whether the pickleball courts at Edison or Marina share ground with the tennis courts is something the City does not say, and its habit of listing them under separate headings with separate counts is the closest thing to an answer. The other thing the page shows is a City willing to write a negative. "(NO LIGHTING)" is not a gap; it is a statement, and an operator that states what a court lacks is one whose silences about surface can be read as real silences rather than oversights.
slots.local_scene: Thirteen verified courts across four City parks, none of them lit, and every one of them stated in a single four-line block on the City's Park Amenities page. Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park hold four courts each; Boardwalk Park holds one. Huntington Beach is the second California city on this site, after Irvine, and the second in Orange County. Nothing was refused: all four parks the City lists with a pickleball court publish here, at the addresses the City pairs with the counts. The distinctive fact about this city is what it says no to. Before this run, stated lighting negatives in prose existed at exactly two venues in the whole directory - Vancouver's Oakbrook Community Park and Cape Coral's Giuffrida Park - and Seattle's GIS layer carries a "No" for nineteen more. Huntington Beach adds four stated negatives in one heading, more than the directory previously held in prose, and it is the first city here where the operator states that no published court is lit. A stated negative is published as "No"; silence is published as "not verified". This city is the clearest example on the site of the difference. What the City does not say is nearly everything else. It publishes no hours for these courts, no price, no surface, no parking and no indoor-or-outdoor answer, so fee_type stays null and the indoor and outdoor breakdowns stay empty. Its Tennis & Pickleball Information page prices reserved tennis courts and never prices or frees a pickleball court, which is why Huntington Beach is not recorded as free. The same page is where organised pickleball appears: OC Racquet Sports offers clinics, camps and private lessons that the City describes in terms of "tennis or pickleball goals", registered through the City's SANDS system or at four community centres. That is the whole of the City's published pickleball scene - four parks, thirteen courts, one heading and a clinic provider. It is thin, and this page says so rather than padding it.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most park around the courts
best_for.text: Edison Park has four pickleball courts, unlit, and appears on more of the City's amenity lists than any other pickleball park in Huntington Beach: restroom, basketball court, handball court, skate park, sports field, tennis courts, volleyball court and walking loop. The Edison Community Center is at the same address and takes registrations for the City's tennis and pickleball programmes.

best_for.heading: Best if you want four courts and no tennis courts alongside
best_for.text: Worthy Park has four pickleball courts, unlit, and is the one four-court venue the City does not list under its tennis heading, so nothing lit at this park competes for attention. The City lists a restroom, a basketball court, a picnic table or shelter, a sports field and a walking loop, and gives the park two addresses; 1831 17th St. is the one paired with the count.

best_for.heading: Best if you are four players who want one court
best_for.text: Boardwalk Park has one pickleball court, unlit, in a park the City lists for an exercise course and a volleyball court and nothing else. One court is one game at a time with no rotation, which suits a group that arrives together and does not suit anyone hoping to find a game. Daylight only, on the City's own statement.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Huntington Beach have?
faqs.a: Thirteen, across four City parks, and every one of them is stated by the City on a single page: four each at Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park, and one at Boardwalk Park. No venue was refused. The City lists no other park with a pickleball court, so thirteen is both the verified count and the City's own total.

faqs.q: Are any of the courts lit?
faqs.a: No, and the City says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. The heading over all four venues reads "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Huntington Beach is the first city on this site where the operator states that no published court is lit, so every court here closes with the daylight.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Huntington Beach?
faqs.a: Not stated, so this site does not say so. The City prices reserved tennis courts - "$9 per hour" on its tennis page, and "$4 per hour" in a separate block on its amenities page - and never prices or frees a pickleball court. Silence on price is recorded as unknown here, not as free.

The City publishes no hours for its pickleball courts. The only timing fact it states is that none of them is lit, which sets the closing time at dusk by default. The "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" hours on the City's tennis page belong to lighted tennis courts at Edison and Marina, not to the pickleball courts.

faqs.q: Why does Worthy Park have two addresses?
faqs.a: Because the City publishes two. Its amenities page pairs the court count with 1831 17th St., and its Tennis & Pickleball Information page lists "Worthy Park 1801 Main Street" among the community centres that take registrations. The count-bearing address is the one published here, and the other is stated on the venue page rather than dropped.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Huntington Beach?
faqs.a: The City never calls any of these courts indoor or outdoor, so these pages publish no indoor or outdoor breakdown for Huntington Beach and there is no indoor or outdoor filter page. That is a gap in the City's record rather than a statement that indoor courts do not exist.

faqs.q: Can I take a pickleball lesson or clinic?
faqs.a: The City's tennis page says OC Racquet Sports runs clinics, camps and private lessons for "your tennis or pickleball goals", with "over 50 classes offered each week", registered through the City's SANDS system or in person at the Edison, Murdy, Marina Park and Worthy Park community centres. Which park's courts host the pickleball classes is not stated.
